name: Image & Video Analysis
summary: Scientific methods for evaluating recorded imagery, including provenance, metadata, camera geometry, frame timing, perspective, parallax, motion analysis, enhancement, compression artifacts and uncertainty.

relationships.context: The PURSUE paper operationalizes the topic's key principle that apparent image motion is not automatically physical velocity.

scienceResearch.intro: Image and video recordings can provide valuable evidence, but what they show depends on the recording system, geometry, metadata, processing history and available context. GreyAlien connects UAP imagery with established methods for evaluating provenance, frame timing, apparent motion, image processing and analytical uncertainty.
scienceResearch.keyPrinciple: What appears to happen in an image is not automatically the same thing as what can be quantitatively established from the image.
scienceResearch.keyPrincipleSupport: Distance, physical size, speed, acceleration, shape, temperature and origin may require additional calibrated measurements, metadata, geometry or independent observations.

foundation.title: Provenance & Authentication
foundation.text: Begin with the source, history and integrity of the media. Authentication can evaluate whether imagery is consistent with its claimed origin or has been altered, but authentication alone does not identify the object shown.

foundation.title: Native Media & Metadata
foundation.text: Original or native files are preferred. Conversion, transcoding, exporting and screen capture can alter visual properties or strip metadata needed to understand timing, sensor settings and acquisition context.

foundation.title: Frame Timing
foundation.text: Reliable motion estimates depend on trustworthy frame timing. A visual impression of rapid movement is not equivalent to a measured physical speed.

foundation.title: Camera & Sensor Geometry
foundation.text: Field of view, focal length, camera orientation, range, lens distortion and image dimensions determine what quantitative measurements can be supported.

foundation.title: Perspective & Parallax
foundation.text: Observer motion and uncertain target range can produce large apparent motion against a distant background. Perspective can also distort perceived size and distance.

foundation.title: Motion Analysis
foundation.text: Estimating true velocity or acceleration requires sufficient geometry, timing and range information. Image-plane motion by itself does not uniquely determine three-dimensional motion.

foundation.title: Image Enhancement & Processing
foundation.text: Stabilization, contrast adjustment, sharpening, interpolation and noise reduction can aid inspection, but processing should be documented, reproducible and evaluated for introduced artifacts.

foundation.title: Compression & Derived Copies
foundation.text: Lossy compression and repeated conversions can obscure detail or create misleading features. Preserve the original bitstream whenever possible and record changes made to working copies.

foundation.title: Measurement & Analytical Uncertainty
foundation.text: Distance, size, speed, acceleration, shape, temperature and origin may require calibrated measurements, metadata, geometry or independent observations that a single recording does not provide.

evidenceClasses.label: Established Science
evidenceClasses.description: Principles or methods supported by established scientific or technical practice.

evidenceClasses.label: Documented Fact
evidenceClasses.description: A factual detail established by an authoritative or primary record.

evidenceClasses.label: Reported Observation
evidenceClasses.description: What an observer or recording is reported to show, without elevating the report to a scientific conclusion.

evidenceClasses.label: Witness Claim
evidenceClasses.description: A source-attributed assertion made by a witness or participant.

evidenceClasses.label: Analytical Interpretation
evidenceClasses.description: A conclusion derived from analysis and dependent on assumptions, available data or methodology.

evidenceClasses.label: Hypothesis
evidenceClasses.description: A proposed explanation that can be evaluated against evidence.

evidenceClasses.label: Speculation
evidenceClasses.description: A proposed conclusion not supported by sufficient evidence for stronger classification.

evidenceClasses.label: Disputed
evidenceClasses.description: A claim or interpretation for which materially different analyses or evidence exist.

evidenceClasses.label: Unknown
evidenceClasses.description: The available information is insufficient to classify the point more precisely.
